objects_built.name: phi_access_log
objects_built.role: Append-only record of each read or write of health data (user, resource, record, time). Not tagged phi, so the logger does not reach itself.

objects_built.name: log_phi_access
objects_built.role: Writes one phi_access_log row; called unconditionally by every object reaching a phi table (enforced by PHI-001).

templates_considered: CONF-012 confidential_tables_tagged: fit; used, scoped with tables to patients and clinical_notes so users.email is not caught
CONF-011 sensitive_fields_marked: fit; used, scoped with tables for the same reason
CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: fit; used with table_tags phi
DATA-010 no_pii_in_responses: fit; used with fields ssn, dob, insurance_member_id
LOG-001 no_sensitive_data_in_logs: fit; used as the template states
CONF-013 views_hide_sensitive: fit; used with no params
VND-001 approved_vendors_only: fit in shape, but the approved list is the owner's decision; used with empty hosts and providers
SEC-011 tls_verification_on: fit; used as the template states
RET-001 audit_log_protected: in the health recipe but needs an audit_log table and an audit function the customer did not ask for at this stage; not used, reported as a gap
RET-002 retained_data_cleaned_up: no retention rule was asked for; not used
SEC-012 no_secrets_in_code: not in the health recipe and no hardcoded credentials were in scope; not used
AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login: overlaps CONF-010 for phi tables; not used to avoid a second auth rule over the whole workspace

rules.covers: Tables holding health data are tagged
Only logged-in endpoints reach health tables
Responses kept free of identifiers (sensitive fields also forbidden by default)
Debug logs do not carry request input or user data
Health data only to approved vendors; empty list reports every outbound call as not yet reviewed until the owner decides
Every object reaching health tables records the access (custom rule; no template)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Audit of edits and deletes of patient records (who changed what), i.e. RET-001 and the audit_changes recipe
Approve which vendors may receive PHI (hosts, providers)
Whether the SSN/DOB chart response should stop returning those fields
Access reviews, training, change approvals, BAAs, encryption at rest, backups, retention age
Runtime data: what is actually stored and sent, and copies between environments
Support agent and ticket summarizer sending patient data to a model provider
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: no check reads prompt content; only provider/host via VND-001

ask_parts_not_covered.part: A PHI field under a name no rule lists (e.g. reason on appointments)

assumptions: patients, clinical_notes and appointments hold health data; customer_notes and users do not (scoped away)
The customer wants the appointments endpoint closed to anonymous callers, which is what the recipe requires; flagged for confirmation
The users table is the only auth table (auth = true)
log_phi_access is called with user_id from $auth.id; the new access row carries no PHI beyond resource and record id
Sensitive attribute syntax {sensitive = true} on a field is what the platform expects; the dry run accepted it
tags = ["phi"] at table level is the tag syntax (matches the endpoints' tags = [...] form)
Empty hosts and providers on VND-001 is accepted by the parser and means every outbound call is unreviewed
confusions: The skill's recipe for health data says the access-record function needs one shared phi tag, and CONF-012 uses a different tag name (confidential) by default; I used phi for both. The skill says to match them, so this is consistent, but the default template tag and the recipe tag differ and that is easy to miss.

The recipe says to add a function that records access and name it in the rule, but it does not say whether the function's own table must avoid the phi tag. I left phi_access_log untagged to avoid a recursive call requirement.

The skill does not show the XanoScript syntax for the sensitive field attribute or for table-level tags. I guessed {sensitive = true} on the field and tags = ["phi"] on the table; the dry run accepted both, but the skill should show the form.

VND-001 needs hosts or providers; with an intentionally empty approved list the template gives no guidance, and I could not tell whether an empty list is the intended way to say 'nothing approved yet'.
CONF-010 and PHI-001 flagged the phi tag as on no table on the live branch; expected because the tag is new in this change, but the warning does not say the tag is being created in this same push.
The LOG-001 template only checks debug.log; the recipe's datadog.log advice is in the limits text but not in the template rule, so I did not add a second rule.
statement.expression_rule for LOG-001 would also catch the clinical_notes debug.log I removed; the template does not say a removed debug line is a better fix than a refactor.
wished_for: A worked example of the sensitive field attribute and table-level tags in XanoScript.
A recipe note saying when to use tables scope versus a tag, since CONF-011 and CONF-012 would otherwise catch the users table's email field.
A short statement of whether an empty approved-vendor list is a valid 'nothing approved yet' state for VND-001.
A template or check that tests whether a patient-facing or AI-agent call sends PHI (prompt contents), since VND-001 only sees the host.
why_confidence: The policies cover the recipe's checkable parts (tagging, marking, login, response fields, logs, vendor list, TLS, access logging) and the dry run is clean, but nothing was evaluated, so I cannot say which findings will fire. Coverage is partial: no audit log (RET-001), no vendor approval (empty list), the patient chart still returns SSN and DOB, and whether PHI is sent to model providers is not checked. HIPAA compliance is not something a policy can establish.
